assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Fully displayed formula
items.clue: A drawing showing every atom and every bond.

items.label: Alkene
items.clue: A hydrocarbon with a carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.stem: Hydrogen adds to ethene. What happens to the carbon–carbon double bond?

options.text: It stays a double bond in the product
It breaks and the molecule splits into two
It is swapped for a bond to a hydrogen atom
It becomes a single carbon–carbon bond

questions.explanation: In addition reactions atoms add across the double bond so that it becomes a single carbon-carbon bond.

questions.stem: A small piece of sodium is added to ethanol. What is observed?

options.text: It fizzes steadily and hydrogen gas is given off
It fizzes gently and oxygen is given off
Nothing happens; sodium reacts only with water
It fizzes and carbon dioxide gas is released

questions.explanation: Alcohols react with sodium to give off hydrogen, more gently than water does.

questions.stem: What happens when ethanoic acid dissolves in water?

options.text: An acidic solution forms, with a pH below 7
A neutral solution forms, as with ethanol
It does not dissolve, being an organic liquid
An alkaline solution forms, from the –OH

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids dissolve in water to give acidic solutions.

questions.stem: Which set of substances react with alkenes by addition across the double bond?

options.text: Hydrogen, water and the halogens
Oxygen, carbon dioxide and nitrogen
Oxygen, sodium and the halogens
Sodium, oxygen and carbonates

questions.explanation: The specification lists hydrogen, water and the halogens as adding across the carbon-carbon double bond.

questions.stem: Ethanol burns completely in air. What are the products?

options.text: Carbon monoxide and water
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Carbon dioxide and water
Ethanoic acid and steam

questions.explanation: Complete combustion of an alcohol gives carbon dioxide and water.

questions.stem: Ethanoic acid is warmed with ethanol and an acid catalyst. What is formed?

options.text: Ethyl ethanoate, an ester, together with water
A salt and water only, as in neutralisation
Carbon dioxide and water, as with a carbonate
Sodium ethanoate and some hydrogen gas

questions.explanation: A carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol to produce an ester; here the ester is ethyl ethanoate.

questions.stem: What conditions are used for the addition of hydrogen to an alkene?

options.text: Ultraviolet light, no catalyst
Steam with a catalyst at 300 °C
Yeast at about 100 °C to speed it up
A nickel catalyst at about 150 °C

questions.explanation: Hydrogenation of an alkene is carried out over a nickel catalyst at roughly 150 °C.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly represents the complete combustion of ethanol?

options.text: C₂H₅OH + 2O₂ → 2CO₂ + H₂O
C₂H₅OH + O₂ → 2CO₂ + H₂O
C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O
C₂H₅OH + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O

questions.explanation: Balanced: two carbon atoms, six hydrogen atoms and seven oxygen atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Which of these formulae is that of a carboxylic acid?

options.text: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
CH₃CH₂OH
C₃H₆
CH₃CH₂COOH

questions.explanation: The –COOH group at the end of the chain makes this propanoic acid.

questions.stem: Ethene is reacted with steam in the presence of a catalyst. What is produced?

options.text: Ethane gas, an alkane, C₂H₆
Ethanol, an alcohol, CH₃CH₂OH
Ethanoic acid, an acid, CH₃COOH
A solution of ethene in hot water

questions.explanation: Water adds across the double bond, so the product of hydrating ethene is ethanol.

questions.stem: What happens when ethanol is added to water?

options.text: It dissolves and the solution has a pH below 7
It floats as a layer and does not mix at all
It dissolves fully, giving a neutral solution
It reacts and oxygen gas is given off

questions.explanation: The first four alcohols dissolve in water and their solutions have a neutral pH.

questions.stem: Bromine water is shaken with ethene. What is seen, and what is formed?

options.text: The orange colour goes as C₂H₃Br and HBr form
The orange colour stays, as ethene is saturated
The orange colour deepens as bromine adds on
The orange colour goes and C₂H₄Br₂ forms

questions.explanation: Bromine adds across the double bond, so the bromine colour is lost and a dibromo compound forms.
